subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub require one shared weekly/monthly popularity contract for publishers, skills, and plugins before adding the visible period tabs?
rationale: Current main has only partial seven-day skill/plugin/package trending, while the RFC leaves maintainer choices around scoring, publisher attribution, backfill, low-activity windows, and snapshot cursor semantics.

options.title: Build shared foundation first
options.body: Add package and publisher temporal rollups plus weekly/monthly snapshot-pinned leaderboards before exposing tabs on any of the three browse pages.

options.title: Ship a narrower surface first
options.body: Expose period controls only where the existing seven-day data is trustworthy, while clearly labeling unsupported publisher or monthly behavior as out of scope.

options.title: Defer period tabs
options.body: Keep the current All/Trending-style browse controls until discovery ranking goals and operational cost are settled.

recommendation.title: Build shared foundation first
recommendation.body: Add package and publisher temporal rollups plus weekly/monthly snapshot-pinned leaderboards before exposing tabs on any of the three browse pages.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest available code provenance for the current browse and leaderboard implementation points to Patrick-Erichsen, despite the shallow-history limitation.
